claims.text: Eutectic high-entropy alloys in the initial state have limited strength.
Eutectic high-entropy alloys in the initial state have limited ductility.
The proposed intervention is the introduction of hierarchical or composite microstructures.
Introducing hierarchical or composite microstructures changes the microstructure architecture.
Control of microstructure can produce a balance between strength and ductility.
Hierarchical or composite microstructures can increase strength relative to conventional eutectic high-entropy alloys lacking those microstructures.
Hierarchical or composite microstructures can increase ductility relative to conventional eutectic high-entropy alloys lacking those microstructures.
The intervention's effectiveness depends on operating conditions and on the ability to control the microstructure during processing.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
